= ====================
 Suman Kumar S/o Late Prem Chandra, Resident of Mohalla- Azad Lane,
 Chaudhary Tola, P.S.- Sultanganj, District- Patna.
Petitioner/s  Versus
1. The State of Bihar.
2. Monika Kumari W/o Suman Kumar, D/o Suresh Prasad Resident of  Mohalla- Azad Lane, Chaudhary Tola, P.S.- Sultanganj, District- Patna.

Opposite Party/s  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Advocate  For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Ramchandra Sahni, APP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH  SINGH  ORAL ORDER 3 03-11-2025 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the complainant and the learned A.P.P.
for the State.
2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in a case in connection with Complaint Case No. 1022 c of 2023, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 494, 420, 406, 109, 323 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code.
However, cognizance has been taken on 19.03.2024 under Sections 498A and 494 of the IPC.
3. As per the prosecution case, the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the petitioner on 27.03.2006.

It is further alleged that in the year 2016 the petitioner started treating the complainant harshly and also started asking for Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.47219 of 2025(3)
dt.03-11-2025 money to do business.
It is further alleged that the petitioner has illicit relationship with a woman namely, Rekha Kumari and in the year 2022, he contracted second marriage with her.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

The petitioner neither demanded any dowry nor tortured the Suman Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154291176/
1 complainant.

entities.text: Suman Kumar vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegation levelled in the complaint petition is false and fabricated and the petitioner has not committed any such offence as alleged in the complaint petition.
The petitioner has not solemnized second marriage with any other girl and merely on suspicion the complainant has lodged this false case.
It is further submitted that the petitioner is the husband of the complainant and he has no concern with the alleged offence.

The petitioner has relied upon the judgment of this Court in the case of "Md. Naimul Haque Ansari @ Naimul Haque Ansari & Ors. Vs.
The State of Bihar, reported in 2006(3) PLJR 182."

sentences.text: Learned counsel has further submitted that Section 498 A of the the Indian Penal Code is triable by the Magistrate.

Learned counsel has further relied on the judgments in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another (2022) 10 SCR 351 and Md. Asfak Alam Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Another passed in Patna High Court CR.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another (2022) 10 SCR 351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Md. Asfak Alam Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: MISC. No.47219 of 2025(3) dt.03-11-2025 Criminal Appeal No (s). 2207 of 2023 arising out of Special Leave Petition (CRL.) No. 3433 of 2023.
The petitioner has got 5 criminal antecedent as stated at para 3 of the bail petition.
5. Learned counsel for the complainant as well as learned APP for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail petition of the petitioner.

6. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances as well as the nature of allegation against the petitioner, let the petitioner named-above, in the event of his arrest / surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, be enlarged on anticipatory bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Patna City, Patna, in connection with Complaint Case No. 1022c of 2023, subject to conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the BNSS, on further condition:
(i) The petitioner is directed to remain physically present before the learned trial Court on each and every date, failing which on two consecutive dates without reasonable cause, the bail bond of the petitioner is liable to be cancelled.
7. If so advised, either of the parties will be at Patna High Court CR.

MISC. No.47219 of 2025(3)
dt.03-11-2025 liberty to make an application before the Court below for referring the matter to the District Mediation Centre for the purpose of reconciliation or one time settlement.
8. This application stands allowed.

(Chandra Prakash Singh, J) Shahnawaz/-
